standard: ISO 53 / DIN 867 basic rack; ISO 54 / DIN 780 modules; DIN 3960 definitions
description: Simpson gear set: two ordinary planetary stages on ONE common sun, with the stage-1 carrier bolted to the stage-2 ring so that carrier 1, ring 2 and the output are a single rigid member. That one coupling is what turns two ordinary stages into a multi-ratio set, and it is modelled as one solid. Tooth flanks are true involutes generated from the DIN 867 basic rack; each stage is an ordinary planetary, so the assembly and neighbouring conditions apply per stage. Every member's angle is solved from the output angle through the 1st-gear mesh relations, so the coupling is computed rather than drawn.
source: ISO 53 / DIN 867, ISO 54 / DIN 780 and DIN 3960 for the tooth form and module series. The topology is the Simpson set; its four ratios are a property of the tooth counts and were solved from a Willis system in exact rational arithmetic, not taken from any one product's table.
